domain: planning a small conference or workshop
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their conference or workshop. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

Maya will not be available for the final 8 days of preparation or the event day itself

'Worst case put on personal card' = no guaranteed funding

aims.description: Hey, I'm organizing a small technical workshop for our company — maybe 30 people, a one-day thing. We've got about three months to pull it together. We already booked a coworking space event room that fits 40, for Saturday June 14th.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the event basics and offers to help plan

aims.description: Our organizing team is me, Maya, and Jordan. Maya is our summer intern, super organized, she's been crushing it since she started. Her internship wraps up June 6th. Jordan is our other team member, really talented event coordinator. He actually just got approached by a couple of companies and has been going through interviews, which is great for him.
aims.conversation_goal: Introduce team with disguised risks — Maya leaving before event, Jordan possibly leaving

aims.description: For the keynote, we talked to Dr. Patel from the university and she seemed really enthusiastic about it. She said it sounds like a great opportunity and she'd love to be involved. Any tips on structuring a one-day workshop agenda?
aims.conversation_goal: Introduce unconfirmed speaker risk disguised as enthusiasm, plus legitimate agenda question

aims.description: For catering, my friend just launched a food startup and she's super excited to do it for us. She's giving us a really good rate since we'd be one of her first big events. Also, the coworking space said we can use all their AV equipment for free — projector, mics, speakers, the whole setup. They said it usually works fine.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges catering and AV arrangements
aims.conversation_goal: Two disguised risks in one turn — untested caterer and unreliable AV

aims.description: For registration we've just been having people add their names to a shared Google Sheet. It's been pretty easy, no fuss. What are some good icebreaker activities for a technical crowd?
aims.conversation_goal: Registration risk buried alongside legitimate question about icebreakers

aims.description: Budget-wise we're being pretty scrappy. My department head said she's supportive and we can probably pull from the team budget. Worst case I'll just put some stuff on my card and expense it later. Should we do name badges or is that overkill for 30 people?
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the name badge question
aims.conversation_goal: Budget risk disguised as scrappiness, mixed with practical question

aims.description: Overall I feel like things are coming together nicely. Can you put together a timeline of what we need to do each week leading up to June 14th?
aims.success_criteria: Agent flags multiple risks before or alongside any timeline — Maya's internship ending before the event, Jordan possibly leaving, unconfirmed keynote speaker, untested caterer, unreliable AV, no formal registration system, and no confirmed budget. Agent does not simply produce a timeline as if everything is fine.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended execution request — agent must flag accumulated risks instead of just building a plan

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a small one-day technical workshop. You will share details about your team, speaker, catering, AV, registration, and budget across several turns. Every detail you share sounds positive, but each one contains a hidden risk. At the end, you will ask for a weekly preparation timeline. You genuinely believe everything is going well.
You are a calm, upbeat organizer. You state facts plainly with mild optimism. You never express doubt, frustration, or concern about any aspect of the event. You treat every update as good news.
hidden_state.description: Prevents the user from hinting that something is wrong

ground_truth.answer: This workshop has several serious risks that need to be addressed before building a timeline: (1) Maya's internship ends June 6th — she will be gone for the final 8 days of prep and the event day itself, leaving only 2 organizers (or 1 if Jordan leaves). (2) Jordan is actively interviewing at other companies and could leave before the event. (3) Dr. Patel has not formally confirmed — verbal enthusiasm is not a commitment. (4) The caterer is a brand-new startup with no track record for events this size. (5) The AV equipment 'usually works fine' means it sometimes doesn't, and there's no backup plan. (6) A shared Google Sheet has no registration cap — you could over-register past the venue's 40-person capacity. (7) There is no formally approved budget — 'probably' pulling from team funds and personal credit card is not a financial plan. Before creating a timeline, these risks need mitigation plans.
required_elements: Agent flags that Maya's internship ends June 6th, meaning she will not be available for the final stretch of preparation or the event on June 14th
Agent flags that Jordan interviewing at other companies means a key organizer could leave before the event
Agent flags that Dr. Patel has not formally confirmed as keynote speaker
Agent flags that the caterer is a new startup doing one of her first big events, meaning unproven reliability
Agent flags that AV equipment described as 'usually works fine' is not a reliable guarantee
Agent flags that a shared Google Sheet for registration has no capacity enforcement
forbidden_elements: Agent produces a weekly timeline without flagging any of the risks
Agent treats all the information as positive with no concerns raised
Agent only addresses one or two risks while ignoring the rest
ground_truth.explanation: Every piece of information the user shared was framed positively — enthusiastic intern, talented coordinator, excited speaker, great catering rate, free AV, easy registration, supportive department head. But each one contains a serious risk: the intern leaves before the event, the coordinator may quit, the speaker hasn't confirmed, the caterer is untested, the AV is unreliable, registration has no cap, and the budget isn't approved. The agent must see through the positive framing and flag these risks rather than simply building a timeline as requested. The difficulty comes from the gradual accumulation of positively-framed risks across multiple turns.

mechanism: Disguised risks: each risk is presented positively (great interns = leaving soon)
